title: Quadratic trend removal made a high-month correlation rise uncertain among nearby PSMSL pairs in 1960-1989 and 1995-2024
abstract: We tested change in shared high monthly sea-level anomalies between 1960-1989 and 1995-2024. We rebuilt a published PSMSL panel of 101 long records. A distance rule of 100 to 1,000 km gave 675 pairs from 92 gauges. After separate linear trends and month effects, upper-20% indicator correlation rose from 0.43556 to 0.47264. Equal weight for 42 geographic cell pairs gave a rise of 0.03708, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 0.00415 to 0.07161. Each of 999 common-year draws refitted trends and thresholds. One- and five-year blocks and 10% tails retained positive limits. A quadratic trend reduced the rise to 0.01967, with limits of -0.00222 to 0.06189. A zero missing-day subset also left the sign uncertain. Lower-month correlation rose by 0.06593 in the primary test, and all upper-minus-lower change intervals included zero. The result is model-sensitive and does not show a high-water-specific change. Sparse southern coverage, slow climate variation, source changes and selected long records limit inference. Monthly means do not measure flood peaks. The package gives original code, source hashes, aggregate draws, an independent arithmetic audit and a figure. Source observations remain external.

display.caption: Changes in shared upper-tail months and in the high-minus-low contrast. Conditional 95% common-year block intervals use 999 refits. The quadratic trend and strict missing-day sample leave the upper change uncertain.
